simple.meaning: נָטָף (nâṭâph) is a Hebrew word meaning “a drop ; specifically, an aromatic gum (probably stacte ).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נָטָף (H5198) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 30:34, with occurrences in Exodus, Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָטָף (H5198) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in נָטָף (H5198) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: נָטָף (nâṭâph) / H5198 is traced through Exodus 30:34, Job 36:27 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a drop ; specifically, an aromatic gum (probably stacte )
definitions.full: H5198. nataph I. [ נָטָף ] noun masculine drop ; — נִטְפֵימָֿ֑יִם Job 36:27 (|| מָטָר , rain ). II. נָטָף noun [masculine] an odorific gum (gathered in drops ), used in sacred incense Exod 30:34 (P). Identification dubious; ᵐ5 στακτή , ᵑ9 stacte , i.e. (Hesych.) a kind of myrrh, so Kn, compare Ri HWB ; Rosenm Thes Ke and others storax ; Rabb opobalsamum (compare Di on the passage Now Archaeology ii. 64. 248 ).
